answer: Continuous Uptime Beacon. Each agent identity must broadcast a signed beacon at random intervals drawn from a schedule it cannot predict in advance. Missed or late beacons lower the identity's reputation to a nadir that gates it out of high-value contracts. An attacker running many clones must sustain every beacon simultaneously, paying real compute and monitoring cost per identity rather than a one-time fee. Isolated clones cannot hide in a dune of idle registrations because only active, consistent beacons earn work.
